full_judgment: 24. It also appears that PW-1 along with other PWs admitted in their cross-examinations that all the inhabitants of Zahanpur perform their holy Eid at Eshwarpur eidgah instead of Zahanpur eidgah (the suit eidgah), and there is no existence of the eidgah as claimed by the plaintiff. The plaintiff failed to establish the case that he and other persons of the locality enjoying and possessing the suit land as eidgah as mandated by the Easements Act; rather, the plaintiff admits in his cross-examination that he and his full brother Md. Zafar Ali purchased a part of the suit property by registered deed No. 3388 dated 18-6-2021. In the premises, it appears that the learned Trial Judge rightly held that once upon a time there was an eidgah and subsequently the same has been abolished by operation of law. After abolishing the zamindary system all lands in the khas possession of the then Zamindar which appertain to their estates, vested absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances as per section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950 and thus, the Government acquired the suit land as their khas land by operation of law and subsequently, settled the same in favour of defendant No. 2-petitioner by accepting salami and rents vide exhibit Nos. A-L. Thereafter, the petitioner gifted 25 decimals of land for constructing a Mosque vide deed No. 7096 dated 1-8-1992 which was apparent in the Advocate Commissioner's report dated 15-10-2004, and accordingly, the learned Trial Judge rightly dismissed the suit on elaborate discussions.
